scope: Proposals only; no TeX edits or build performed. Only paragraphs changed by the reference audit are targeted. Rendered-line savings require the final build; word savings are a rough guide.

proposals.old_text:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) scales outcome
supervision through executable validation \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}.
Prior work reports declining policy entropy and output diversity during
reasoning RL \citep{cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}. A conventional verifier
records only correctness: repeated copies and different successful outputs
receive the same scalar reward. We show that accuracy can rise while support
over distinct verified output modes contracts. Repeated sampling and
verifier-guided selection use multiple proposals
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime,cobbe2021training,lightman2023lets}.
Concentration on one correct mode leaves fewer verified alternatives for a
selector; it need not reduce pass@$K$ at fixed per-sample correctness.
proposals.proposed_text:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains from executable
correctness feedback \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}. Reasoning RL can reduce policy
entropy and output diversity \citep{cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}.
A correctness-only reward treats repeated and distinct successes alike; we
show that accuracy can rise while verified-mode support contracts.
Repeated sampling supplies proposals for verifier-guided selection
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime,cobbe2021training,lightman2023lets}.
Concentration leaves fewer verified alternatives, without necessarily reducing
pass@$K$ at fixed per-sample correctness.

proposals.old_text:
Repeated sampling and verifier-guided selection depend on the proposal
distribution \citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}. Prior work reports
reduced sampled output diversity under RLHF or reasoning RL
\citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity}, declining policy entropy
\citep{cui2025entropy}, and reduced high-budget problem coverage in tested RLVR
models \citep{yue2025rlvrlimit}. These measures differ from within-prompt
execution-key breadth. Semantic clustering infers when generations express the same answer
\citep{farquhar2024detecting}. \mb{} instead lets accepting execution define
the equivalence relation, yielding an exact behavioral key.
proposals.proposed_text:
Sampling-based selection depends on the proposal distribution
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}. Prior work measures reduced output
diversity under RLHF or reasoning RL \citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity},
declining policy entropy \citep{cui2025entropy}, and reduced high-budget problem
coverage for tested RLVR models \citep{yue2025rlvrlimit}. These metrics differ from
within-prompt execution-key breadth. Semantic clustering infers answer
equivalence \citep{farquhar2024detecting}; \mb{} defines keys by accepting execution.

proposals.section: related work: replay and persistent memory
proposals.old_text:
Experience replay reuses past experience and can mitigate forgetting
\citep{lin1992selfimproving,rolnick2019replay}; RLEP reuses successful
reasoning trajectories \citep{zhang2025rlep}. ReplayDr.GRPO instead stores one exemplar per canonical executed key and
samples uniformly over keys, making equal retention an explicit target rather
than depending on how often each success occurs. Novelty search rewards behavioral novelty
\citep{lehman2011novelty}, while MAP-Elites retains one elite per behavior-descriptor
cell \citep{mouret2015illuminating}. Our replay bank uses the execution key
as the descriptor inside a policy-gradient update.
proposals.proposed_text:
Replay reuses experience and can mitigate forgetting
\citep{lin1992selfimproving,rolnick2019replay}; RLEP replays successful reasoning
trajectories \citep{zhang2025rlep}. ReplayDr.GRPO retains one exemplar per executed
key and samples keys uniformly, regardless of discovery frequency.
Novelty search rewards behavioral novelty \citep{lehman2011novelty}; MAP-Elites
retains one elite per descriptor cell \citep{mouret2015illuminating}.
Our replay bank uses execution keys as descriptors within policy-gradient updates.

proposals.old_text:
A binary reward identifies success but is indifferent among successful keys.
GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath} and Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding}
center that reward within each sampled group, assigning every
correct response the same task credit regardless of its execution key. Key
frequency is therefore the remaining asymmetry: a common correct mode appears
in more updates, while an absent mode supplies no direct signal.
proposals.proposed_text:
GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath} and Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding}
center binary rewards within sampled groups, giving correct responses equal
task credit regardless of execution key. Common correct modes therefore appear
in more updates; absent modes supply no direct signal.

proposals.old_text:
When successes are scarce, their weight increases; failures receive $-1$.
All-failure and all-success groups have zero task advantage. This is the
centered binary MaxRL estimator \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}. Lemma~\ref{lem:maxrl-mean}
derives its on-policy mean objective over budgets $k=1,\ldots,G-1$.
It is applied only to fresh on-policy rows.
proposals.proposed_text:
Applied only to fresh on-policy rows, this centered binary MaxRL estimator
\citep{tajwar2026maxrl} assigns failures $-1$ when $m>0$ and zero advantages
to all-failure or all-success groups. Lemma~\ref{lem:maxrl-mean} derives its
mean objective for $k=1,\ldots,G-1$.
